source_review.notes: Reviewed all ten references. Determinate process networks were checked against Kahn's indexed IFIP record; concurrency-model critique against Lee; static region/effect determinism and explicit safe nondeterminism against the two DPJ papers and HotPar paper; system-enforced execution against DMP, CoreDet, and Determinator; current reduction language against OpenMP 5.2; and floating-point scope against IEEE 754-2019. Four ACM DOI targets returned publisher HTTP 403 and two IEEE DOI targets returned accepted HTTP 202 after resolution; metadata and scoped claims were checked through indexed institutional/primary records. Kahn metadata, USENIX sources, and OpenMP documentation resolved directly. No inaccessible quotation is used.

evidence: The DAG proof uses deterministic base inputs and node functions with noninterfering effects and topological induction.

Stable reduction and ordered-commit proofs fix index/tree/sequence independent of schedule and use induction to obtain one root/state.
